inputs.text: Three months after the mandate, Uttar Pradesh still hasn’t given brick kiln operators a clear path to environmental clearance. That failure isn’t just red tape: when compliance is opaque, middlemen can profit and workers and nearby communities are left exposed to the costs. Kiln owners say they’re willing to get the additional approvals and already hold State Pollution Control Board approvals tied to water and air standards. The state must make the rules transparent and workable, meet recent court decisions, and protect both the environment and the livelihoods dependent on the industry. Clean air and water should not come at workers’ expense—or be used to excuse institutions from making fair, accountable rules.
